title: Three PDO products had lower means in 2020-2024 than in all January-start five-year windows within 1950-2019
abstract: We compared three Pacific Decadal Oscillation (PDO) products on common dates. The 2020-2024 mean was below all 66 January-start five-year means within 1950-2019 in each product. After scaling by each pre-2020 monthly standard deviation, recent means were -1.495 for NCEI ERSSTv5, -1.204 for the PSL legacy table and -1.742 for the PSL SST ensemble. An affine calibration fitted to 1950-2019 left recent NCEI-minus-product gaps of -0.433 and 0.213 index units. Calibration with 1980-2019 reduced both gaps and placed them within earlier five-year residual ranges. Thus the low mean holds across these definitions, while its size depends on product and calibration period. The ensemble file names ERSSTv6 although its web page names ERSSTv5. Shared observations, revised histories, a selected recent period and overlapping historical windows limit inference. The result does not validate climate-model tail probabilities or establish a new regime. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, calibration draws and an arithmetic audit are included. External records remain outside the package.

display.caption: Three products have low recent means, but their calibrated magnitudes differ. Red bars give calibration-only intervals; gray bars give earlier five-year residual ranges.
